title: J-K flip-flop

sources.document: TI The TTL Data Book for Design Engineers, 2nd ed. 1976, section 5 (pin assignments and function tables)
TI The TTL Data Book for Design Engineers, 2nd ed. 1976, section 6 (gate and flip-flop data sheets)

pins.name: J'
pins.text: inverted J input; must be grounded if not used

pins.name: K'
pins.text: inverted K input; must be grounded if not used

functions.text: Q is the stored bit (low while PR and CLR are both low).
Q' is the inverse of the stored bit (low while PR and CLR are both low).

rules: J = J1 AND J2 AND NOT J'; K = K1 AND K2 AND NOT K'
PR low, CLR high, CK low: Q = 1, Q' = 0 at once
PR high, CLR low, CK low: Q = 0, Q' = 1 at once
PR low, CLR low (CK don't care): Q = 0 and Q' = 0 (table prints L* L*); not stable, does not persist when PR and CLR return high
Preset or clear can occur only when CK is low
PR high, CLR high, rising edge of CK: J=0 K=0 hold; J=1 K=0 Q=1; J=0 K=1 Q=0; J=1 K=1 toggle
PR high, CLR high, CK low: hold

unknown: Typical preset and clear propagation delays: the table gives the maximum (50 ns) only.
notes: The 7470 function table prints PR=L, CLR=L as Q = L, Q' = L (marked nonstable); the 7472/7474/7476 tables in the same book print H H for that case. The datasheet gives no minimum propagation delays; the path-delay function uses 0 ns for the minimum.

stored.name: FF1
stored.next: FF1 = (J1 AND J2 AND NOT J' AND NOT FF1) OR (NOT (K1 AND K2 AND NOT K') AND FF1)
stored.whenSetAndClear: neither wins: Q and Q' are both LOW while both act (table prints L* L*); not stable
